newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysian Railway to evict squatters in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian Railway to evict squatters in Singapore.

text.p: The Malaysian railway company KTM Berhad is to take legal action to evict people its says are occupying land it owns in Singapore, lawyers said on Thursday.
Lawyers acting for KTM said they would serve notice to people illegally occuping more than 100 plots of land.

The announcement coincided with a souring of ties between the two neighbours after news reports, denied by the Malaysian government, that Kuala Lumpur had decided to freeze all new bilateral ties with Singapore.
Malaysia Minister of Works S.Samy Vellu said a culture and sports agreement was the only casualty of the suspension.
Relations hit a low after Singapore elder statesman Lee Kuan Yew called the south Malaysian state of Johor "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".
Lee has twice apologised for the remark but the issue has refused to die.
"We will go ahead and serve notice from tomorrow. There are more than 100 plots of land that have been occupied," KTM lawyer said.
KTM owns more than 200 hectares (500 acres) of land in Singapore on a 999-year lease.
The KTM land bank in Singapore was earlier highlighted by Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohammed as one of the difficult issues in its relations with Singapore.
Singapore and Malaysia are in talks to relocate KTM's station in Singapore but have not agreed on a new site. Mahathir said Singapore was pressing Malaysia to give up the land.
"We have a right to run the KTM trains on that land for 999 years, but they try to pressure us by various means to move out so that we don't use Tanjong Pagar," he said.
The Tanjong Pagar station, next to Singapore's central business district, is considered prime real estate.

Under an accord signed in 1990 by Lee when he was prime minister and former Malaysian finance minister Tun Diam Zainuddin, the goverments agreed to exchange the 16-hectare Tanjong Pagar land with a plot of equal value.

The KTM railway line in Singapore runs for about 25 km (15.5 miles) north-south across the island. KTM has rights to a reserve of 66 feet (20 metres) on either side of the track, according to Malaysian law.
KTM cancelled a news conference scheduled to take place on Thursday to explain its decision to evict the squatters.
